concepts.learning_objective: Explain what the Vedas are and how their hymns were preserved orally over many generations.
Describe the Vedic ideas of ritam, the many names of one reality, and the call for unity among people.
Identify the janas of early Vedic society and the clues (raja, sabha, samiti) about how they were governed.
Recognise the variety of professions mentioned in the Vedic texts.
Explain the Upanishadic ideas of brahman and atman and why they lead to the idea that all beings are connected.
Interpret the stories of Shvetaketu, Nachiketa and Gargi and the value they place on asking questions.
Identify Vedanta and Yoga as schools that grew out of the Vedas and formed the foundations of Hinduism.
Narrate the main events in the life of Siddhartha Gautama leading to his enlightenment.
Explain the Buddha's teachings on ignorance, attachment, ahimsa and inner discipline.
Describe the Sangha and the values expressed through the Jataka tales.
Describe the life of Mahavira and the lessons of Jain stories such as that of Rohineya.
Explain the Jain principles of ahimsa, anekantavada and aparigraha.

topics.title: Many Schools, One Trunk
topics.ncert_sections: Spread of teachings; Charvaka; shared concepts

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how monks and nuns spread their teachings and the evidence left in monasteries and rock-cut caves.
Explain the diversity of schools of thought, including the Charvaka school, and why the term 'religion' is considered limiting.
Identify the concepts shared by the Vedic, Buddhist and Jain schools that form the 'trunk' of Indian culture.
Define a tribe and explain folk and tribal traditions as oral traditions of India.
Explain how tribal belief systems regard nature as sacred while also holding a concept of a supreme being.
Analyse the two-way interaction between tribal traditions and Hinduism and its result of mutual enrichment.
